quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. Even with a locked rear wheel, you can control your motorcycle if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you stay out of other vehicles' blind spots, see and be seen better, avoid hazards, avoid wind blasts, and escape danger. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely so they can move.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it doesn't cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This keeps you in control of your motorcycle's direction.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting it.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal, but if you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
Has a seat even with your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets you reach the ground with your feet while seated. Keep your feet on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is also called:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like using the brakes. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: May help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: May help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: A bright-colored helmet is recommended. It protects your head in a crash and helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after starting out.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a dangerously slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible over slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of the following is NOT important?

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fits snugly, and has no cracks or damage. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you maximum stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars tightly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road when safe. Do not brake hard, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to keep your balance.
Keep your speed steady to stay on the road.
Do not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery roads when possible. If you cannot avoid them, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: To be effective, a face shield should NOT:
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be scratch-free, allow you to see to the sides, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight shield can fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: The front brake provides what percentage of a motorcycle's braking power?

options.text: Should only be used on wet roads.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear your tire go flat. Tire failure usually shows up as a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride.
